candidates.source_name: Ephrem the Syrian / Commentary on Deuteronomy
candidates.source_attribution: Ephrem the Syrian, Commentary on Deuteronomy, on 34:1-12. NPNF Series 2, vol. 13. PD. Cf. Jude 9, Mt 17:3; Tewahedo liturgical witness: Astə'arǝgya-Mussē.
candidates.draft_body:
Ephrem the Syrian Commentary on Deuteronomy (c. 365 AD)

On Moses' burial 'in a valley in the land of Moab, over against Bethpeor: but no man knoweth of his sepulchre unto this day' (Deu 34:6), Ephrem reads the divinely-hidden grave as the canonical Old-Testament anchor of Jude 9's account of the archangel Michael's dispute with the devil over Moses' body — preserved in the Assumption of Moses tradition received by the Ethiopian canon. The hidden grave prepares Moses for his Transfiguration appearance with Elijah (Mt 17:3, Lk 9:30-31), suggesting a translation-pattern parallel to Enoch (Gen 5:24) and Elijah (2 Ki 2:11). Tewahedo Astə'arǝgya-Mussē (Translation of Moses) commemorates this hidden-grave tradition; Deu 34:6 + Jude 9 + the Buhe Transfiguration form the canonical triple-witness of Moses' translated-glorified state.
